h1: Charter Bus Rental in Shelton, CT for Offices and Events
heroIntro: Shelton sits on Route 8, a few miles north of the Merritt Parkway, and that parkway is the first thing to know about moving a group here. Connecticut bans buses from it. Any trip toward Stamford or New York City runs on I-95 instead, and that changes the drive time. Cascade Charter Bus arranges charter buses, minibuses and Sprinter vans in Shelton for office shuttles along Bridgeport Avenue, wedding guests staying at the Courtyard Shelton, school outings to Jones Family Farms and group days in New York. We plan the route a bus is allowed to drive before we quote it.

services.title: Corporate and Employee Shuttles
services.text: Shelton is an office town. Hubbell runs its headquarters from Waterview Drive, and the business parks along Bridgeport Avenue hold thousands of desks. Most of our work here is for companies: daily shuttles between an office and the Bridgeport or Stratford train stations, rides to off-site meetings, and client groups coming up from New York. An all-day loop usually books as a minibus — it stages more easily outside a building and goes easier on the hourly rate.

services.title: School and Field Trips
services.text: Two places in Shelton fill with school groups every year. Jones Family Farms — a 400-acre farm in the White Hills, worked by the same family since 1848 — takes classes for berries in summer and pumpkins in October. The Sports Center of Connecticut on River Road packs ice rinks, mini golf, bowling and laser tag under one roof. A school bus is the cheapest seat in town for short local runs; on a long day out, a coach buys you a restroom and luggage space.

services.title: Wedding Shuttles
services.text: Wedding guests usually stay at the hotels along Bridgeport Avenue — the Courtyard Shelton among them — while the venue tends to sit out in the hills or along the Housatonic. A loop between hotel and venue means nobody hunts for the place in the dark, and nobody drives after the reception. Send us the venue address and the time the reception ends. We check the driveway on a map, pick a vehicle that fits it, and plan the last run around that.

services.title: New York City Day Trips
services.text: Midtown sits about 65 miles from Shelton. A car's map runs you down the Merritt Parkway; buses can't take it, so the trip moves to Route 8 and I-95 instead. Figure about two hours each way, longer on a weekday morning. One coach also means one meeting point in the city whichever way you're headed — and in Manhattan a bus may only stop in marked bus zones, so we agree on the drop-off well before the trip.

destinationsHeading: Top Charter Bus Destinations in Shelton

destinations.name: Jones Family Farms
destinations.text: A 400-acre farm in the White Hills, worked by the same family since 1848. Groups come for strawberries and blueberries in summer, pumpkins in the fall and cut-your-own trees in December, and there's a winery on site for adult groups.
destinations.tip: October and December weekends jam the farm roads, and they're narrow to begin with. Book the group visit with the farm ahead of time and ask where a bus should unload.

destinations.name: Indian Well State Park
destinations.text: A wooded state park on Lake Housatonic with a 15-foot waterfall, picnic groves and a lifeguarded beach in summer. Camp groups and company picnics claim it all season.
destinations.tip: On hot summer weekends the lot fills and the park shuts its gate behind the last car. Get there before 10 a.m., and check bus parking and group fees with Connecticut State Parks before you commit.

destinations.name: Sports Center of Connecticut
destinations.text: The family entertainment center on River Road: double-decker ice rinks, mini golf, bowling, laser tag and a driving range. Youth hockey teams, birthday parties and school reward trips land here, especially in winter.
destinations.tip: Big lot right off Route 110. The bus unloads at the main entrance and the driver parks on site until your group is ready to go.

destinations.name: Veterans Memorial Park and the Riverwalk
destinations.text: Downtown's riverfront park draws summer concerts, food trucks and the city fireworks, with a Saturday farmers' market next door in the warm months. The old factory buildings around it now hold restaurants, an easy dinner stop for a group.
destinations.tip: Streets near the river are tight, and some close on event nights. We drop a block or two back and set the pickup time before the crowd lets out.

destinations.name: New York City
destinations.text: Groups head into Manhattan for Broadway, museum days and holiday trips. It's about 65 miles by road, on I-95 once the Merritt ban bumps you off the parkway. Rush hour makes the drive longer than a car's map suggests.
destinations.tip: Leave before 7 a.m. or after 9:30 a.m. to miss the worst I-95 traffic. Buses in Manhattan may only stop in marked bus zones, so we set the drop-off nearest your first stop.

faqs.q: Can a charter bus use the Merritt Parkway?
faqs.a: No. Connecticut bans buses from both the Merritt and Wilbur Cross parkways. Any trip from Shelton toward Stamford, Westchester or New York City runs on I-95 instead.

faqs.q: How long does a bus take from Shelton to New York City?
faqs.a: About two hours to Midtown in normal traffic, on Route 8 and I-95. Weekday mornings stretch that, which is why we usually aim to leave before 7 a.m. or after 9:30 a.m.

faqs.q: Can you run a daily shuttle for our Shelton office?
faqs.a: Yes. Recurring loops on a fixed schedule are normal work for us — an office park to the Bridgeport or Stratford train station, say, with one invoice for the business.

faqs.q: Which vehicle is best for a field trip to Jones Family Farms?
faqs.a: A school bus, for most classes — it's the cheapest seat for a short local trip. Two things to do first: book the farm visit, and ask where a bus should unload.

faqs.q: Is a wheelchair-accessible vehicle available?
faqs.a: Yes, on request. Accessible vehicles need advance notice, usually at least 48 hours, so mention it when you ask for the quote and we'll confirm the vehicle before anything is booked.

title: Charter Bus Rental in Kailua-Kona | Cascade Charter Bus
metaDescription: Book a charter bus, minibus or Sprinter van in Kailua-Kona, HI for Kona airport transfers, cruise pier pickups, weddings & coffee farm tours. Free quote 24/7.
h1: Charter Bus Rental in Kailua-Kona, HI for Groups & Events
heroIntro: Kona moves groups differently from the mainland. Flights land at Ellison Onizuka Kona International Airport, about seven miles north of town on Queen Kaahumanu Highway. Cruise passengers come ashore by tender boat at Kailua Pier, one boatload at a time. And many of the coffee farms above town sit on roads too narrow for a bus. Cascade Charter Bus arranges Sprinter vans, minibuses and motorcoaches through licensed island operators for resort transfers, shore excursions, weddings and farm tours. Tell us where the group is going before you tell us how many are coming. On this island, the road usually picks the vehicle.

services.title: Airport and Resort Transfers
services.text: Kona's airport is open-air and small, and a group of twenty with luggage can swamp the taxi line. One vehicle waiting at arrivals is simpler and usually cheaper per person. We run transfers to the hotels along Ali'i Drive, to Outrigger Kona Resort and Spa at Keauhou, and north to the Kohala Coast resorts. Send us the flight numbers. The driver follows the flights, so a late arrival doesn't leave your group standing on the kerb.

services.title: Coffee Farm and Sightseeing Tours
services.text: Last August a coffee farm in Kailua-Kona asked us to move more than a hundred guests for a tour. The farm road was too narrow even for a minibus, so we ran five Sprinter vans in rotation. No single operator had five vans free that day, so we brought them together from several. We also sent water coolers, because August here is humid and a farm tour is mostly outdoors. The owner thanked us for the coolers as much as the vans.

services.title: Wedding Shuttles
services.text: Most Kona weddings happen at oceanfront resorts and private estates along Ali'i Drive and Keauhou, with guests spread across several hotels. Ali'i Drive is a two-lane coast road with very little parking, so a shuttle loop saves your guests a long walk in formal clothes. We plan the last run back for after the reception ends, not before. Ask the venue how wide the entrance is. Estate driveways here often suit a Sprinter van better than a bus.

vehicles.reason: The only choice for most coffee farm roads.
Airport and resort transfers for 20 to 32 guests.
Large groups staying on the main highways.

destinationsHeading: Top Charter Bus Destinations in Kailua-Kona

destinations.name: Kailua Pier and Ali'i Drive
destinations.text: Cruise ships can't dock in Kona. They anchor in Kailua Bay and send passengers to the pier by tender boat, so a shore-excursion group arrives in waves. The pier sits at the north end of Ali'i Drive, a short walk from the shops and restaurants.
destinations.tip: Build the pickup window around the tender schedule, not the ship's arrival time. There is a taxi and pickup lot just west of the pier where vehicles wait.

destinations.name: Kona Coffee Farms
destinations.text: The coffee farms sit on the slopes above town, around Holualoa and south toward Captain Cook. Many welcome groups for tours and tastings. The farms are working land, and their access roads are often narrow, steep and unpaved.
destinations.tip: Ask the farm what size vehicle can reach it before you book. In most cases that means Sprinter vans running in rotation. Bring water for outdoor tours in summer.

destinations.name: Pu'uhonua o Honaunau National Historical Park
destinations.text: Known as the Place of Refuge, this national park is about 22 miles south of Kailua-Kona. It protects a royal compound and a sanctuary enclosed by a massive stone wall. Groups usually pair it with a coffee farm stop on the way back.
destinations.tip: The road down from the highway is steep and winding. Commercial tour vehicles need National Park Service authorization, so confirm it with us when you book.

destinations.name: Hulihe'e Palace
destinations.text: This former royal vacation home stands on Ali'i Drive in the middle of town, across from Mokuaikaua Church, the oldest Christian church in Hawaii. Both are easy stops for a walking group and take about an hour together.
destinations.tip: There is no bus parking at the palace. We drop near the pier and your group walks five minutes along the seawall. The driver waits off Ali'i Drive and returns at an agreed time.

destinations.name: Kona International Airport
destinations.text: The airport is about seven miles from Kailua-Kona town on Queen Kaahumanu Highway. The terminal is open-air, with gates you reach on foot across the tarmac, so groups come out quickly once bags arrive.
destinations.tip: Share flight numbers for every arrival. If your group lands on several flights, we plan one pickup per cluster of flights so nobody waits more than an hour in the heat.

mapPins: Pu'uhonua o Honaunau National Historical Park

nearby.heading: Other Areas We Serve on the Kona Coast

faqs.q: How do I check that a Hawaii charter operator is licensed?
faqs.a: Look at the side of the vehicle. Hawaii requires certified passenger carriers to show their name and their Public Utilities Commission number on both sides. Every operator we use in Kona is certified.

faqs.q: Can you pick up cruise passengers at Kailua Pier?
faqs.a: Yes. Ships anchor in the bay and passengers arrive by tender, so we time the pickup to the tender schedule. Vehicles wait in the lot just west of the pier.

faqs.q: Can a bus reach the Kona coffee farms?
faqs.a: Usually not. Most farm roads are too narrow for a bus or minibus, so we use Sprinter vans and run them in rotation for larger groups.

faqs.q: How far is Kona airport from town?
faqs.a: About seven miles, or 15 to 20 minutes, along Queen Kaahumanu Highway. The Kohala Coast resorts are farther north, so tell us which hotel you are staying at.

faqs.q: Should we book early for IRONMAN week?
faqs.a: Yes. The IRONMAN World Championship fills Kona every October, and the island has a fixed number of vehicles. Ask for transport as soon as your team's travel dates are set.

title: Charter Bus Rental in Alexandria | Cascade Charter Bus
metaDescription: Book a charter bus or minibus in Alexandria, MN for Arrowwood Resort weddings, Minneapolis airport transfers, winery tours & team travel. Free quote, 24/7.
h1: Charter Bus Rental in Alexandria, MN for Groups & Events
heroIntro: Most groups coming to Alexandria have the same problem before they arrive. There are no airline flights into town, so everyone lands at Minneapolis-St. Paul, about two hours down I-94. Cascade Charter Bus arranges charter buses, minibuses and Sprinter vans to close that gap, and to move groups around once they are here. We handle wedding shuttles to the lake resorts, conference transport for Arrowwood Resort, winery outings to Carlos Creek and team travel for tournaments. Tell us where your guests land and where they sleep. We plan the pickups and send a quote the same day.

services.title: Lake Resort Wedding Shuttles
services.text: The Alexandria area has more than 350 lakes, and most summer weddings here happen beside one of them. Guests stay in town or at a resort, the ceremony is on a lawn by the water, and the road in is often a narrow lake lane. Tell us about that road before you tell us the headcount. Sometimes two minibuses reach a venue that one coach can't. We run loops from the hotels and plan the last ride back for after the dance floor closes.

services.title: Minneapolis Airport Transfers
services.text: Alexandria Regional Airport handles private and business aircraft only, so airline passengers fly into Minneapolis-St. Paul. The drive is about 130 miles and takes two hours. For a wedding party or conference group landing on several flights, one coach with luggage bays and a restroom is far easier than a line of rental cars on I-94. Give us the flight numbers. We group the arrivals into one or two pickups so nobody waits long at the terminal.

services.title: Conference and Retreat Transport
services.text: Arrowwood Resort and Conference Center is where most company meetings in Alexandria take place, and many attendees arrive without a car. We bring groups up from Minneapolis, run evening shuttles into town for dinner on Broadway, and take teams to outings on the lakes or at Carlos Creek Winery. Send one schedule for the whole event. We return a transport plan with pickup times and vehicle sizes, and a single invoice your accounts team can process.

services.title: Winery and Brewery Tours
services.text: Carlos Creek Winery, just north of town, is the stop most groups ask for. It runs events through the year, including a grape stomp weekend each September. A minibus with a professional driver lets the whole group taste without anyone watching their glass. We can add a brewery or a lakeside lunch stop and set the route around your booking times. For bachelorette groups and birthdays, ask about a party bus instead.

destinationsHeading: Top Charter Bus Destinations in Alexandria

destinations.name: Arrowwood Resort and Conference Center
destinations.text: Arrowwood sits on Lake Darling, a few miles northwest of downtown. It is the area's main venue for conferences and large weddings, with an indoor waterpark, golf and a marina that keep families busy between sessions.
destinations.tip: Coaches can pull up to the main entrance to unload. Ask the resort's events team where a bus should wait during your function, since the front drive gets busy at check-in time.

destinations.name: Carlos Creek Winery
destinations.text: One of Minnesota's biggest wineries, Carlos Creek has tasting rooms, live music and a brewery on the same grounds. The grape stomp in September is its busiest weekend and draws visitors from across the state.
destinations.tip: Book group tastings ahead and tell the winery you are arriving by bus. On festival weekends, expect to be directed to a separate bus unloading area away from the car park.

destinations.name: Lake Carlos State Park
destinations.text: About 10 miles north of Alexandria, the park has a sandy swimming beach, hiking trails and a group camp used by scouts, church groups and school classes. It is a good day out for youth groups in summer.
destinations.tip: Vehicles entering a Minnesota state park need a permit. Call the park office before your visit to arrange bus entry and to ask which lot is closest to your group site.

destinations.name: Runestone Museum and Big Ole
destinations.text: Downtown, the Runestone Museum displays the Kensington Runestone, found near here in 1898. A short walk north is Big Ole, a 28-foot Viking statue that every visiting group ends up photographing. The Central Lakes Trail starts beside him.
destinations.tip: Broadway is the main street and has kerb space for a quick unload. The driver then parks nearby and your group walks between the museum and the statue.

destinations.name: Minneapolis-St. Paul International Airport
destinations.text: MSP is about 130 miles southeast of Alexandria, almost all of it on I-94. Plan on two hours in good conditions. Winter storms and Friday cabin traffic heading north from the Twin Cities can both add time.
destinations.tip: The airport has two terminals several miles apart. Check which one each airline uses, and send us the flight list so we can plan pickups at the right doors.

faqs.q: Can you fly into Alexandria, MN?
faqs.a: Not on an airline. Alexandria Regional Airport serves private and business aircraft only. Most visitors fly into Minneapolis-St. Paul, about two hours away, and take a bus or car from there.

faqs.q: Can you pick up wedding guests at Minneapolis airport?
faqs.a: Yes. Send us the flight numbers and we group the arrivals into one or two pickups. A full-size coach with luggage bays suits the two-hour drive best.

faqs.q: Can a full-size bus get down a lake resort road?
faqs.a: Sometimes not. Many resort and cabin roads around the Alexandria lakes are narrow. Tell us the venue and we check the access. Two minibuses often work where one coach can't.

faqs.q: Do buses run to Alexandria in winter?
faqs.a: Yes. I-94 is cleared quickly after snow, but storms can slow or close it for a few hours. We build spare time into winter trips and keep in touch with the driver on the day.

faqs.q: How far ahead should we book for a summer wedding?
faqs.a: Four to eight weeks ahead for June through September. Saturdays go first, and the same vehicles serve several lake towns across central Minnesota.

h1: Charter Bus Rental in Park City, UT for Groups & Events
heroIntro: Most Park City group trips start about 35 miles away, at Salt Lake City International Airport. From there the road climbs I-80 through Parleys Canyon, and in ski season that stretch gets snow and slow traffic. Cascade Charter Bus arranges charter buses, minibuses and Sprinter vans for ski groups heading to Park City Mountain and Deer Valley, wedding parties staying around Old Town, and company retreats at the resort hotels. Send us your flights, your lodging and your headcount. We match the vehicle to the roads it has to drive, and your quote comes back the same day.
servicesHeading: Group Transportation Services in Park City

services.title: Ski Group and Airport Transfers
services.text: Flying a ski group into Salt Lake City? One coach carries everyone and the gear. A full-size motorcoach has luggage bays under the floor for ski and board bags, so nothing rides in the aisle. We time the pickup to your flights, then drop at the base your group is using: Park City Mountain Village, Canyons Village, or Snow Park Lodge at Deer Valley. Staying the week? Book the return run at the same time so the seats are held.

services.title: Wedding Shuttles
services.text: Park City weddings tend to spread out. The ceremony is on the mountain, dinner is on Main Street, and guests sleep anywhere from Kimball Junction to Deer Valley. Parking is tight at most venues, and nobody wants guests driving canyon roads after a reception. A minibus running loops between the hotels and the venue fixes both. Ask your venue where a bus can load before you book. Some lodge driveways and Old Town streets can't take a full-size coach.

services.title: Corporate Retreats and Conferences
services.text: Company retreats fill Park City's hotels in every season, not only winter. We run airport transfers for teams arriving on different flights, evening shuttles between the hotel and dinner on Main Street, and half-day outings to Utah Olympic Park, where the 2002 Winter Games bobsled track still runs. One person at your company sends us the schedule. We turn it into a pickup plan with times, vehicle sizes and a single invoice.

destinationsHeading: Top Charter Bus Destinations in Park City

destinations.name: Historic Main Street
destinations.text: Main Street is where most groups eat, shop and spend the evening. It is steep, narrow and busy, and the city keeps large vehicles off it: oversized vehicles need a special parking permit, and for-hire vehicles need a drop-and-load permit between 5 p.m. and midnight.
destinations.tip: The free loading zone on Swede Alley takes vehicles up to 35 feet. A 45-foot coach won't fit, so for big groups we plan a drop at the edge of Old Town or split the group into minibuses.

destinations.name: Deer Valley Resort
destinations.text: Deer Valley is skiers-only and has two base areas. Snow Park is the original base on the Park City side. East Village is the newer one, just off U.S. 40, with about 1,200 day-skier parking spaces and a gondola.
destinations.tip: Snow Park Lodge has a marked skier drop-off zone at the front of the lodge. Tell us which base your lessons or lift tickets are booked from, because the two are a long drive apart by road.

destinations.name: Park City Mountain
destinations.text: Park City Mountain is one resort with two separate bases: Mountain Village, next to Old Town, and Canyons Village, a few miles north near Kimball Junction. Groups often book lodging at one and lessons at the other without noticing.
destinations.tip: Check your confirmation for the base name before the trip. Mornings between 8 and 9:30 are the busiest time at both bases, so we set pickups a little earlier and agree one meeting point for the ride home.

destinations.name: Utah Olympic Park
destinations.text: Built for the 2002 Winter Games, the park is still a working training site. Groups come for the museums, to watch ski jumpers train, and for team activities that include rides on the bobsled track. It sits on a hill above Kimball Junction, close to I-80.
destinations.tip: The access road climbs steeply. Book your group visit with the park first and ask where buses should unload. We pass those directions to the driver.

destinations.name: Salt Lake City International Airport
destinations.text: Nearly every Park City group flies in here. The drive is about 35 miles and takes 40 to 45 minutes in clear weather. Snow in Parleys Canyon or Friday afternoon traffic can add half an hour or more.
destinations.tip: Send us every flight number. If your group lands over several hours, two smaller vehicles on staggered pickups often cost less than one coach waiting at the kerb.

nearby.heading: Charter Bus Rental Near Park City

faqs.q: How long is the bus ride from Salt Lake City airport to Park City?
faqs.a: About 40 to 45 minutes in clear weather. The drive is roughly 35 miles on I-80 through Parleys Canyon. Allow extra time in snow and on Friday afternoons in ski season.

faqs.q: Can a full-size charter bus drop our group on Main Street?
faqs.a: Not directly. Park City keeps oversized vehicles off Main Street without a special permit, and the free loading zone on Swede Alley only takes vehicles up to 35 feet. We plan a nearby drop or use minibuses.

faqs.q: Is the Sundance Film Festival still held in Park City?
faqs.a: No. The festival's last Park City edition was in January 2026, and it moves to Boulder, Colorado from 2027. Late January is still peak ski season here, so vehicles book up early.

faqs.q: Which ski base should the bus take us to?
faqs.a: The one printed on your lesson or ticket confirmation. Park City Mountain has Mountain Village and Canyons Village. Deer Valley has Snow Park and East Village. They are miles apart by road, so check before travel day.

faqs.q: How far ahead should we book a bus for ski season?
faqs.a: As soon as your dates are firm. Christmas week, Presidents' Day weekend and Saturdays in March are the hardest dates to find a vehicle. For other weeks, two to four weeks ahead is usually enough.

services.title: Pittsburgh Airport Transfers

Send us the flight times and where your group is meeting, and the driver watches for delays on the day.

services.title: Church and Religious Groups
